summary: Completed backend regression, public API checks, and end-to-end UI testing for registration, dashboard, claim intake, demo analysis, citations, search/detail, decisions, history, and policy rules.

critical.issue: Meals policy text states eligibility up to 75 USD per person, but deterministic validation uses policy.limit=600 and accepted a 100 USD Meals claim as Pending Review without LIMIT-EXCEEDED.

action_items: Align the Meals policy limit used by deterministic validation and stored policy data with the displayed 75 USD per-person rule; add a regression test for an amount over 75 USD.
Clean up temporary API/UI test accounts and claims from the preview SQLite database if required before stakeholder review.
critical_code_review_comments: POLICY-01 data is internally inconsistent: Meals text says 75 USD per person while the limit field is 600; the validator trusts the inconsistent field, allowing claims that contradict the visible rule.
seed_data_creation: Created temporary reviewer accounts and test claims through the public registration/UI/API flows; no pre-seeded credentials were available. This data remains in preview storage.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All requested primary flows passed. Re-test Meals over-limit behavior after correcting the 75-vs-600 policy mismatch; also exercise clarification and override persistence after that fix.
rca of the issue: POLICY defines Meals limit as 600 while its text says 75 USD per person. policy_for() and deterministic() use the numeric limit field, so validation never flags a 100 USD Meals claim. Update the canonical policy model/limit semantics and test the boundary explicitly.
